expectations.text: Recommends designing only 5-8 key screens that establish visual style
expectations.evidence: Explicitly prescribes 5-8 key screens: landing/hero, dashboard/main view, detail page, form/input, empty state, settings — explains why each matters for style definition

expectations.text: Focuses on visual direction rather than documenting every state
expectations.evidence: Emphasizes that Figma screens are style guides not specs — AI generates states, responsive variants, and edge cases from the visual direction

expectations.text: Explains how Figma MCP shares design data with AI for code generation
expectations.evidence: Walks through Figma MCP workflow: select frame, MCP reads design properties (colors, spacing, typography, layout), AI generates matching code

expectations.text: Teaches the handoff process from Figma to code via AI
expectations.evidence: Step-by-step handoff: design key screen in Figma, use MCP to read it, prompt AI to implement, visual review, iterate

expectations.text: Sets up an efficient workflow that avoids over-designing
expectations.evidence: Establishes 'design minimal, generate maximal' principle with concrete time estimates: 2-3 hours in Figma vs 2-3 days traditional
